source_review.review_method: independent original DOM/XML/metadata assertions; source-proven failures inspected locally

authors.scope: complete captured author list and order

references.scope: all captured reference text, numeric tokens and independently decoded DOI, in source order

prose.scope: Selected source prose and heading runs in order; decimal points, signs, case and scientific script roles retained; editorial punctuation normalized. Citation/footnote markers are separately scoped.

figures.scope: Captured caption runs preserve scientific symbols; captions bound to their own source image or original shared panel group. Explicit inline assets also checked against available retained prose neighbors.

tables.scope: Source data rows and column assignments checked within owned output table groups without reuse; scripts and fractions retained. Captured float/callout and gallery placement contracts applied; one-column boxes and semantic lists retain text checks.

notes_and_statements.scope: all captured table notes and bounded data/code availability statements

tex.scope: source TeX including scripts/fractions; whitespace, display style and equivalent delimiters normalized

mathml.scope: numeric content, identifiers, critical operators and minimum subscript/superscript/fraction/root structure per original expression; not full AST equivalence

citation_targets.scope: original callout targets map to the same ordered bibliography and DOI; not a proof of all final inline anchors

image_identity.scope: each emitted image has original URL/rendition identity; every captured figure with an image maps back to that same figure DOM or same-page viewer entry; captured binaries use separate collection tests

limitations: MathML facts do not establish complete formula AST equivalence or bitmap contents.
Prose/caption text normalization does not establish typographic punctuation equivalence; table cells and reference numeric tokens have separate checks.
Citation target tests bind original callouts to output bibliography; final inline anchor structure is covered only by publisher-specific cases.
No structured formula in the selected original; bitmap/externally loaded formulas have only captured index/link evidence.
Supplementary material: same-paper index and links only; removed payloads and placeholder images are not content evidence.
No captured image response with an image media type registered here; image claims are limited to original index/URLs.

source_objects.method: Source DOM/XML nodes only; no production extraction or rendering output. Object indexes follow source selection, grid cells refer to source row/cell indexes.

cells: Terms These only partially overlap and are not synonymous. Regenerative event: a self-driven event (waveform) involving a positive feedback loop, e.g., between voltage and current (or calcium and voltage, or calcium-induced calcium release). Spike: a voltage transient; in the wider world, many shapes and sizes; generally agreed it must go up then down (or vice versa, i.e. be self-terminating). In neuroscience, by convention, a spike usually has a threshold of some kind across which the response jumps qualitatively/substantially in size/shape, in a biologically/computationally significant manner. Threshold can be voltage or an input variable such as glutamate, or indeed it can be multidimensional. Threshold does not need to be fixed (e.g., strength-duration trade-offs, relative refractory periods) and may need to be teased out: It may not be apparent in all input-output (I-O) relations, even though the voltage waveform is spike-like and very similar to a supra-threshold waveform from another I-O relation that does exhibit a clear threshold (see section on Sharpness of Threshold and Spike-Sigmoid Duality below). Action potential (AP): a membrane-voltage transient that normally results in some distinct biological action (e.g., a muscle contraction or release of neurotransmitter); usually, but not necessarily, all-or-none. The term action potential has a broader meaning than many neuroscientists may assume: for example, cardiac action potential = slow spike + plateau; Nitella (algae) chloride-mediated action potential; negative-going action potentials in Ascaris (roundworm) pharyngeal muscle ( Byerly & Masuda 1979 ). All-or-none: an event that, once started (i.e., by some threshold being exceeded), proceeds by itself to completion; if not started (i.e., threshold not reached), a substantially different (smaller/briefer) event results. However, all-or-none does not mean completely stereotyped in size and shape (or threshold). Electrogenic: causing an electrical change. Includes positive feedback, negative feedback (such as sag, undershoot, after-hyperpolarizations), and delayed combinations of the two (e.g., oscillations, pacemaking).
